sub_topics: CJP's connection to Manolo Lopez: first met in early 2007, three years ago; invited to join First Philippine Holdings as independent director with Don Oscar M. Lopez and Don Eugenio 'Gabby' L. Lopez III

The Meralco independent directorship offer: in early May 2008, Manolo called CJP in New York where he was 'doing my APostolate with my grandchildren'; offered a second ID seat in Meralco; only two candidates for two vacant IDs -- no difficulty being elected on May 27, 2008

The Meralco corporate war: nine in the morning to twelve midnight -- 'the longest and most tumultuous stockholders' meeting I have ever attended'; a group challenged Lopez control in a 'bruising proxy and legal battle that went all the way to, and was won by the Lopez group, in the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court'

Board meetings under fire: 'the leader of the minority block harangued Meralco Chairman Manolo Lopez and repeatedly accused him and his family of various alleged misdeeds'; 'coupled with the constant prayers of Mrs. Maritess Lopez, Manolo's shield as a gentleman and presiding officer was tested and found impregnable'

Character under pressure: 'though provoked many times by hostile language and sometimes unpredictable behavior, Don Manolo never lost his temper. He was always cool to a fault, bearing every unkind word with admirable serenity, never retorting with intemperate words. When he could no longer bear the heat, he would leave the conference room for a while to cool off and always came back with a clear mind.'
Victory: 'his main critic has left the board and the company. And Don Manolo won the bruising corporate war with equanimity, grace and fortitude.'

Character portrait: 'courageous but not pugnacious, prudent but not tentative, humble but not wimpy. He is firm with his decisions, responsible with his actions and cadenced with his language. Never vindictive... Jesus-like self-restraint that earned him the esteem and respect of everyone.'

Populist by choice: 'a glutton for work and a master of teamwork. Though privileged by birth, he is populist by choice. A firm believer in corporate social responsibility, he always finds ways to help the rank and file employees with health plans, production incentives, performance-based compensation, stock options and other innovative benefits. He motivates them by his personal example of integrity and devotion to duty. He is equally at ease with the common employees as he is with the executives of the company and the titans of Philippine business.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered May 21, 2010 as a birthday tribute for Manuel 'Manolo' M. Lopez at his Copa celebration -- requested by Leony de la Llana, the 'brains and baton-wielder' -- this address by CJP draws on three years of close observation as an independent director. He first met Manolo in early 2007 (two months after retiring as CJ), when Manolo and the Lopez patriarchs Oscar M. Lopez and Gabby L. Lopez III offered him the First Philippine Holdings ID over lunch. In early May 2008, Manolo called CJP in New York -- 'where I was doing my APostolate with my grandchildren' -- and offered him a second ID in Meralco. CJP was elected on May 27, 2008, which turned out to be 'the longest and most tumultuous stockholders' meeting I have ever attended' (9 AM to midnight): a group challenged Lopez control in 'a bruising proxy and legal battle that went all the way to, and was won by the Lopez group, in the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court.' Board meetings continued to be difficult -- the minority leader harangued Chairman Manolo repeatedly -- but 'Manolo's shield as a gentleman and presiding officer was tested and found impregnable,' aided by the constant prayers of his wife Maritess. His technique: when he could no longer bear the heat, he would leave the room, cool off, and return with a clear mind. His character under fire: 'courageous but not pugnacious, prudent but not tentative, humble but not wimpy... Never vindictive... Jesus-like self-restraint that earned him the esteem and respect of everyone.' Victory came with 'equanimity, grace and fortitude.' The tribute's governing formulation: 'though privileged by birth, he is populist by choice' -- helping rank-and-file employees with health plans, incentives, stock options, equally at ease with common employees and business titans.
